plan.contextChunk: This figure sets three side-by-side panels, (a), (b), and (c), showing one small undirected graph and two ways of storing it. Panel (a) draws the graph as five gray circles numbered 1 through 5, with 1 at the upper left, 2 at the upper right, 3 at the far right, 4 at the lower middle, and 5 at the lower left, joined by seven straight edges: 1-2, 1-5, 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4, and 4-5. Panel (b) gives the adjacency-list form as a vertical array of five gray cells indexed 1 to 5, each holding a pointer arrow into a horizontal chain of two-field records whose right field is either an arrow onward or a diagonal slash marking the end. Row 1 chains 2 then 5; row 2 chains 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 chains 2 then 4; row 4 chains 2, 5, 3; row 5 chains 4, 1, 2. Panel (c) gives the adjacency matrix as a bordered five-by-five grid of zeros and ones with rows and columns both headed 1 through 5, zeros along the diagonal and entries symmetric across it. Laying the picture beside the two tables lets a single edge be found three ways, and it makes plain that each undirected edge is stored twice.

interactionPlan.concept: An undirected graph can be stored as an adjacency list or an adjacency matrix, and both representations record each edge twice — once for each endpoint — while encoding exactly the same relationships as the picture.
elements: Panel (a): five gray circular nodes labeled 1-5 (1 upper left, 2 upper right, 3 far right, 4 lower middle, 5 lower left)
Panel (b): vertical array of five gray header cells indexed 1-5, each with a pointer arrow
Panel (b): adjacency-list record chains — row 1: 2→5; row 2: 1→5→3→4; row 3: 2→4; row 4: 2→5→3; row 5: 4→1→2 — each record a two-field box with an onward arrow or a diagonal slash terminator
Panel (c): bordered 5×5 adjacency matrix of 0s and 1s, row and column headers 1-5, zeros on the diagonal, symmetric across it
highlight styling for selected edges, list records, and matrix cells

interactions.teaches: One undirected edge is stored twice in each representation — clicking an edge in the graph (or a 1 in the matrix) highlights the two adjacency-list records (u in v's list and v in u's list) and the two symmetric matrix cells (u,v) and (v,u)

interactions.label: Focus representation
interactions.teaches: The three views are interchangeable encodings of the same neighbor relationships — focusing one representation while a vertex is selected shows that its neighbor set is identical in every form

interactions.label: Add / remove edge 1-3
interactions.teaches: Adding or removing one undirected edge always means four coordinated changes: one line in the graph, two list records, and two symmetric matrix entries — the redundancy is structural, not incidental

demo_steps.title: Three views, one graph
demo_steps.narration: The same five-vertex, seven-edge graph appears as a picture (a), an adjacency list (b), and an adjacency matrix (c). Every relationship visible in one panel is present in the other two.

demo_steps.title: Trace one edge
demo_steps.narration: Click the edge 1-2: it lights up in the graph, the record '2' in row 1 and '1' in row 2 of the list, and matrix cells (1,2) and (2,1) — the edge is stored twice in each table, once per endpoint.

demo_steps.title: Focus a single representation
demo_steps.narration: Switch focus to the adjacency list alone: row 2 holds 1, 5, 3, 4 — exactly the four neighbors of vertex 2 that the graph shows as four incident lines and the matrix shows as four 1s in row 2.

demo_steps.title: Add an edge
demo_steps.narration: Press add for edge 1-3: a new line appears in the graph, '3' joins row 1 and '1' joins row 3 of the list, and cells (1,3) and (3,1) flip to 1 — four updates for one conceptual edge.

demo_steps.title: Remove it again
demo_steps.narration: Removing the edge reverses all four changes at once, confirming that the representations stay consistent only because each undirected edge's two copies are always updated together.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because the graph is undirected, every edge {u,v} is stored twice in both representations — v in u's list and u in v's list, and a 1 at both (u,v) and (v,u) — so the matrix is always symmetric and the lists' total length is 2|E|.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three panels side by side on white. Panel (a): gray filled circles with black numerals, thin black edges, arranged with 1 upper-left, 2 upper-right, 3 far right mid-height, 4 bottom-middle, 5 bottom-left; edges 1-2, 1-5, 2-5 (diagonal), 2-3, 2-4 (vertical), 3-4, 4-5. Panel (b): five stacked gray header cells with index numerals 1-5 to their left, each arrow pointing right into a chain of two-compartment record boxes (value in left compartment, pointer arrow or diagonal slash in right); chains per the element list, laid out horizontally with rows aligned to their header. Panel (c): bordered square grid with column headers 1-5 above and row headers 1-5 left, entries 0/1, diagonal all 0, symmetric. Use a single warm highlight color (e.g., amber) for the selected edge's line, its two list records, and its two matrix cells simultaneously; dim non-focused panels when a representation focus is chosen. Panel captions (a), (b), (c) centered beneath each panel.
